# Bintje (01, engineer) — SPD-039

## Brief
Objective: a redirection or tee target that zsh reads as a glob using its own operators, parenthesised alternation `(a|b)` and the numeric range `<n-m>` (also `<->`, `<n->`, `<-m>`), is captured as the word zsh opens and checked as every file it can open, so a member cannot write a protected file through one (Laws 1 and 5). Where the hook cannot tell what zsh opens, it refuses a member and checks Spud against every possibility. Red-first.

The hole (proposal 32 from SPUD-034/Atlantic; `spud ticket show SPD-039` has the evidence): shell_tokens and separate_redirects use shlex punctuation, so in `echo x > (ledger|x)/tickets/SPD-001.md` the `(` starts a subshell and the captured target is `/tickets/SPD-001.md`, and in `echo x > ledger/tickets/SPD-<1-1>.md` the `<` becomes an input redirection and the target is `ledger/tickets/SPD-`; each maps outside the protected roots and a `**` member's write is silent, while zsh 5.9 writes ledger/tickets/SPD-001.md (and every match of an open range). bash rejects both as syntax errors, so the divergence is zsh-only.

Settle with real-shell probes (zsh -f, zsh with the options of the Bash tool's shell on this Mac, which sets `nobareglobqual`, and bash 3.2; in the scratchpad) and pin each with a test:
1. Where zsh reads `(` and `<` as glob syntax rather than punctuation: inside or at the start of a redirection target word, a tee argument, a word after a command name; `<n-m>` only when it matches the range form; `(` only where a word can continue. Tokenize so that in those positions the word zsh sees is kept whole, without changing how bash-valid lines tokenize (every existing test stays green). If the tokenizer cannot do this without a large rewrite, the safe fallback is detection: a target position followed by `(`, or a `<` glued to a word that forms a range, makes the target unknown (refused for a member, every reading checked for Spud). State which you chose and why.
2. Expansion: extend SPD-034's bounded matcher (bounded_glob, brace_expand, neutralize_quoted_globs, deglob) to alternation (nested, with `/` not allowed inside a group in zsh; probe it) and numeric ranges (open ends, leading zeros), under the same scan and match caps. Quoted operators stay literal.
3. Qualifiers and flags: with bareglobqual on (zsh default) a trailing `(.)`, `(/)`, `(N)` is a glob qualifier and `(N)` turns on nullglob for that pattern; on this Mac's Bash tool it is off. Decide how the hook treats a trailing parenthesised group (both readings checked, or refused for a member) and pin it. `(#i)`, `^`, `~` need extendedglob, which is off here; keep them under SPD-034's documented limit unless the fix covers them for free.
4. cd targets: SPD-030 makes a glob cd target unfollowable; check that `cd (ledger|x)` and `cd SPD-<1-2>` are unfollowable too rather than mis-tokenized into a subshell or redirection.
5. The same words in command position (`(cd x)`, `cmd <file`) keep their current meaning; bash-only lines (`cat <(git push)`, `diff <(a) <(b)`, `>(tee x)`) keep SPD-030's handling.

Out of scope: writes by arbitrary programs, cd into an unenterable directory (SPD-037, next), Spud's relative redirection after an unfollowable cd (SPD-035), extendedglob and bash extglob patterns beyond what item 3 decides, native rules (SPD-033). File a proposal for anything else larger you find.

Deliverables (only these paths): `bin/**`, `tests/**`. Never `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/`, `ledger/`, `reports/`, `docs/`.

Read first: `spud ticket show SPD-039`; `spud member show SPUD-034/Atlantic` (the expander and its decisions); `spud member show SPUD-030/Elba` (the tokenizer and ShellWalk); `spud member show SPUD-036/Huckleberry` (the review corpus); in bin/spud_ledger.py: `shell_tokens`, `separate_redirects`, `newlines_as_separators`, `split_substitutions`, `ShellWalk`, `analyse_segment`, `neutralize_quoted_globs`, `deglob`, `brace_expand`, `bounded_glob`, `cd_target`, `bash_reason`; tests/test_hooks.py `GlobRedirectTest`, `ShellModelTest`, `BashHookCase`; tests/helpers.py.

Constraints: the hook budget holds: measure PreToolUse(Bash) median of 15 before and after, same payloads (a plain redirection, an alternation redirection, a git write), interleaved with a scratchpad copy of the unchanged bin/, and put both numbers in the result. The live hooks run the ledger root's bin/spud on main, not this worktree's copy; probe with a scratch SPUD_HOME as the tests do, never against the live ledger. Shell probes that write run in a scratchpad directory only, never with a pattern that can match a real repository file. The live Bash hook refuses git writes for you and any command naming the ledger state directory, and the harness may refuse shell text naming git that it cannot show stays in the worktree: put such payloads inside Python test code. Run the suite from this worktree in the background: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (485 tests, about three minutes). Any `claude -p` probe passes `--model haiku`.

Done when: tests in tests/test_hooks.py that failed on the unchanged code now pass, covering the ticket's two evidence commands and the open range for a `**` member, a narrow-glob member and Spud; nested alternation; a range with leading zeros; tee arguments; a trailing qualifier-shaped group as decided; the cd cases; and controls that stay as they are: `(cd x)`, `cmd <file`, `cat <(...)`, a quoted `(a|b)` in a deliverable target, an alternation matching only deliverables, `2>&1`, `> /dev/null`. The whole suite is green; latency and every decision with its shell probe are in the result.
